channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyz Cabinet Approves Amendments to Kumtor Investment Agreement
item.description: The Kyrgyz Cabinet of Ministers has approved amendments to the revised investment agreement for the Kumtor gold mine. The changes address Centerra Gold's exit from the project and aim to ensure uninterrupted operations. This follows a December 2023 agreement to terminate a previous environmental and investment pact.

item.title: Border Congestion Persists Due to Fuel Smuggling from Kazakhstan to Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Congestion at the Kazakhstan-Kyrgyzstan border has resurfaced due to the illegal transport of cheaper gasoline from Kazakhstan to Kyrgyzstan, where it is sold at higher prices. This practice causes significant delays for regular travelers, with the price difference per liter of AI-92 fuel being around 200 tenge.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Enhances Government Services with Proactive Provision
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is reforming its public service delivery system, expanding the powers of the Ministry of Economy and Commerce. A key change involves developing a proactive service provision model, allowing citizens to receive services without needing to file applications. The ministry will also oversee outsourcing and quality control of these services.

item.title: Kazakhstan Explores AI for Enhanced Budget Planning and Control
item.description: Kazakhstan's President has proposed using artificial intelligence to improve the quality of treasury fund planning and management. The aim is to prevent unnecessary and inefficient spending, with AI offering new possibilities for budget coordination. The Ministry of Finance is tasked with creating a treasury information system and integrating it with state management information systems.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Establishes Lifetime Monthly Stipends for Olympic and World Champions
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has set lifetime monthly stipends for Olympic, Paralympic, and Deaflympic Games champions and medalists, as well as world champions in Olympic sports. The amounts range from 30,000 soms for first place to 20,000 soms for third place and world champions. Stipends are awarded for a single highest achievement.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Three-Year Moratorium on Micro and Small Businesses
item.description: Kazakhstan's President has proposed considering a three-year moratorium on micro and small businesses starting January 1, 2027. This initiative aims to reduce administrative burdens, allowing entrepreneurs to operate stably, increase production capacity, and implement new projects. The proposal also includes expanding SME participation in public procurement.

item.title: Astana Police Launch Investigation into Reports of Two Girls' Deaths
item.description: Astana police have initiated an investigation following social media reports of two girls, reportedly aged 13, dying in the Esil district. While preliminary information suggests the girls were 13, this has not been officially confirmed. A criminal case has been opened.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Budget Revenues Reach 669.6 Billion Som Over 10 Months
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's republican budget revenues totaled 669.6 billion som in January-October, exceeding the plan by 17.3 billion som. The Tax Service collected 288.5 billion som, and the Customs Service secured 155.6 billion som. Business activity index rose to 58.7 points in October.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Inflation Expectations Reach 10-Year Low
item.description: Kazakhstan citizens perceive inflation at 9%, the lowest since 2016, according to a National Bank-commissioned survey. Perceived inflation has been below 10% for three consecutive months. Official statistics show annual inflation at 9.2% in October. Expectations for the next 12 months also dropped to 9.8%.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks High in Global Indices for Power, Digital Services, and Innovation
item.description: Kazakhstan has achieved high rankings in global indices this year. It placed 34th in the 'Most Powerful Countries 2026' ranking by World Population Review and 24th in the UN's e-government survey, leading CIS countries. Kazakhstan also ranked 10th globally for its online government services index.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Tightens Rules for Company Liquidation and Re-registration
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has amended regulations for registering, re-registering, and liquidating legal entities. A key change requires checking for tax, insurance, and customs debts before a company can be closed. Re-registration now mandates disclosure of beneficial owner details, including nationality and personal identification numbers.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Regional Development Initiatives Following Presidential Address
item.description: Information groups are touring Kazakhstan to explain the President's priorities. In Ulytau region, officials discussed digital transformation, AI development, and improving living standards. A 'People's Construction' program aims to modernize social infrastructure, creating new jobs and improving access to education and healthcare.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Median Wage Growth Slows, Gender Pay Gap Widens Significantly
item.description: Kazakhstan's median salary is projected to reach 345,900 tenge by 2026, more than doubling since 2021. However, growth rates are decelerating. The gender pay gap has widened considerably, with men earning 383,700 tenge and women 311,700 tenge by 2026, a fivefold increase in the difference.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Faces Espionage Allegations, Raising US-China AI Security Concerns
item.description: Allegations of a Chinese national attempting to gather intelligence on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have escalated into a national security issue for the US. US lawmakers have requested explanations, while China denies the accusations. An internal investigation is underway, impacting Nvidia's stock price.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches 'Clean Kazakhstan' Environmental Campaign, Emphasizing Sustainable Lifestyle
item.description: The traditional 'Unity - For a Clean Kazakhstan' ecological campaign has begun in the Karaganda region. Over two thousand people participated in cleaning and landscaping efforts. President Tokayev stressed that 'Clean Kazakhstan' should become a lifestyle, promoting environmental responsibility and civic order.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's CEC Clarifies Electronic Signature Collection for Presidential Candidates
item.description: The Central Election Commission of Kyrgyzstan has reiterated the procedure for collecting voter signatures for presidential candidates via the 'Tunduk' app. Candidates need at least 30,000 signatures, collected electronically via cloud digital signatures or on paper. The electronic collection system allows authorized representatives to view signature counts and voter distribution.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Develops Interactive Map of State Property
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has developed an interactive map of state property as part of its digitalization efforts. The modernized state property registry, launched in collaboration with the 'Kyzmat' State Enterprise, provides real-time data on state assets acquired since independence. The map and registry will be fully operational from January 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Economy Grows 4.5% in First 10 Months of the Year
item.description: Kazakhstan's GDP saw a real growth of 4.5% in January-October, an increase of 0.3 percentage points from the previous period. The non-resource sector was the main driver, expanding by 5.6%. Industrial production rose by 3.5%, with manufacturing growing by 9.3%, particularly in machinery, pharmaceuticals, and construction.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Abolishes Visa Requirements with Seychelles, President Signs Law
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has officially abolished visa requirements for short-term stays with the Seychelles. President Sadyr Japarov signed the ratification law for the agreement, which was initially signed on May 11, 2026. The agreement allows citizens of both countries to visit each other without prior visa arrangements. The law takes effect 10 days after its publication.

item.title: Two Sentenced to Life Imprisonment for Murder of Former Banned Tajik Party Member
item.description: A court in Tajikistan's Sughd region has sentenced two residents of Isfara to life imprisonment for the murder of Mannon Sodikov, a former member of the banned Islamic Renaissance Party. The convicted individuals, Ehson Boboev and Yusuf Sharifov, have appealed the verdict, deeming it unjust and excessively harsh. Boboev previously served in law enforcement agencies.

item.title: Seven Irrigation Wells to Be Launched in Bazar-Korgon District
item.description: Seven new irrigation wells are planned to be launched in the Bazar-Korgon district to improve water supply. Water has been successfully tested from a new well in the Kyzyl-Ay area. The project is funded by capital investments and aims to resolve irrigation water issues for local farmers.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Economy Accelerates Growth to 4.5% in First Ten Months
item.description: Kazakhstan's GDP grew by 4.5% in the first ten months of 2026, a slight acceleration from the previous period. Non-resource sectors drove growth, particularly manufacturing, which saw a 9.3% increase. Key contributors included pharmaceuticals, metal products, and machinery manufacturing, according to the Ministry of National Economy.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Approves Unified Registry for State and Municipal Services
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has approved a unified registry for state and municipal services, according to the Ministry of Economy and Commerce. The registry details each service's name, responsible body, conditions, payment procedures, and expected outcomes. Service administrators must update information within ten working days.

item.title: Kazakhstan Implements New Centralized Internet Control System
item.description: A new regulation approved by the National Security Committee chairman will centralize internet control, extending it to mobile operators and hosting companies. Previously, control primarily involved intercity and international communication operators. This move aims to improve telecommunication network management, raising concerns about information freedom and privacy.

item.title: France Investigates Iran's Alleged Role in Supermarket Refrigerator Cyberattack
item.description: French intelligence services have implicated Iran in cyberattacks that disrupted hundreds of supermarket refrigerators in October. Paris prosecutors have launched a judicial investigation into the leader of the Iranian group Shahid Kaveh, citing the use of Persian language and Iranian IP addresses as evidence. France is seeking international arrest warrants.

item.title: Kazakhstan Official Proposes Temporary Loan Freeze for Families with Newborns
item.description: A representative of Kazakhstan's People's Council, Murat Abenov, has proposed a temporary freeze on loans for families with newborns, citing a sharp decline in birth rates attributed to financial difficulties. He suggests implementing interest-free loan holidays for new parents and stricter regulation of microfinance organizations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Mandates Employers to Adjust Wages Based on Inflation
item.description: Employers in Kyrgyzstan are now legally obligated to increase wages in line with inflation. This new regulation applies to both private companies and state organizations. President Sadyr Japarov signed the amendments into the Labor Code, introducing this mandatory adjustment mechanism.

item.title: Tajikistan's Central Bank Offers 100 Million Somoni, Receives 37 Million in Bids
item.description: The National Bank of Tajikistan's credit auction on November 3 saw participants bid for 37 million somoni out of a 100 million somoni offering. Bid volume increased significantly from the previous auction but remained below the available amount. The weighted average rate was 7.01% annually.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Launch ElpayKG Payment System by 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to launch the ElpayKG payment system in 2027, aiming to enhance financial market digitalization and the digital economy. Presented at FinConference 2026, the system is developed by the Interbank Processing Center, operator of the national payment system Elkart. Cybersecurity and digital services were key discussion points.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Proposal to Invite Russia to Turkic States Organization Sparks Debate
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's proposal to invite Russia as an observer to the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) has surprised many. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov supported the initiative, calling it "understandable and appropriate." However, a former OTS secretary general questioned Russia's eligibility, citing its treatment of its own Turkic peoples.

item.title: West Kazakhstan Police Seek Ten HIV-Positive Individuals Who Discontinued Treatment
item.description: Police in West Kazakhstan are searching for ten individuals with confirmed HIV who have stopped their antiretroviral therapy and medical follow-ups. Health authorities requested police assistance to locate them. Currently, 755 people with HIV are registered in the region. In the first nine months of 2026, 44 new HIV cases were reported.

item.title: Two Sentenced to Life in Prison for Murder of Former Islamic Party Activist in Tajikistan
item.description: A court in Tajikistan's Sogd region has sentenced two men to life imprisonment for the murder of Mannon Sodikov, a former member of the banned Islamic Renaissance Party. The verdict was reportedly issued in mid-October, but only recently became public. Both defendants have appealed the sentence, deeming it unfair and excessively harsh.

item.title: Afghanistan Energy Week 2026 Kicks Off in Kabul to Address Energy Challenges
item.description: Afghanistan Energy Week 2026 began in Kabul on November 9th, bringing together investors, businesses, financial institutions, and development partners. The two-day event, co-organized by the UN Development Programme and the Afghanistan Chamber of Commerce and Investment, aims to discuss solutions for the country's energy sector.

item.title: UN Calls for Urgent Action at Climate Change Conference in Turkey
item.description: The international climate change conference, COP31, began in Antalya, Turkey. UN officials urged global nations to accelerate efforts against global warming, stating current progress is insufficient. The conference will address greenhouse gas reduction and clean energy until November 20th.

item.title: Israeli President Assigns Government Formation Task to Netanyahu's Rival
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has officially tasked Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the National Unity party and a rival to Benjamin Netanyahu, with forming a new government. Eisenkot has 28 days to secure support from at least 61 parliamentary members.

item.title: Kazakhstan Raises Tax Control Threshold for Mobile Transfers to 1.56 Million Tenge
item.description: Starting November 10, 2026, Kazakhstan will increase the monetary threshold for tax control on mobile transfers for individuals. The limit rises from 1.02 million to 1.557 million tenge over three consecutive months. This change, outlined in a finance ministry order, applies when transfers are received from 100 or more different senders in each of three months, exceeding 360 monthly calculated indices.

item.title: World Bank: Uzbekistan's poverty rate significantly decreased due to wage and employment growth
item.description: The World Bank reports a significant drop in Uzbekistan's national poverty rate, from 17% in 2021 to 5.8% in 2025, with a further decrease to 3.6% by late 2026. Approximately 3.7 million people escaped national poverty. Higher wages and increased employment were key drivers of this progress.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers New Pasture Use Law for Ecotourism and Agriculture
item.description: Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber is reviewing a bill to expand pasture land usage. The proposed law would permit activities like ecotourism, beekeeping, and medicinal plant cultivation. It also introduces new usage norms, categories, and an electronic platform, 'E-yaylov,' for digital monitoring using AI and satellite data.

item.title: Uzbek-Russian Media Forum in Tashkent Discusses Digital Transformation and Cooperation
item.description: The third Uzbek-Russian media forum in Tashkent serves as a platform to elevate information cooperation between the two countries. Discussions focus on modern media trends, digital transformation, AI, information security, and content creation. Experts highlighted the evolving role of media as a societal influencer and the need for new approaches in technology and professional skills.

item.title: New Wakhan Corridor Road to China Raises Questions for Pamir Kyrgyz and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Afghanistan's Taliban government opened a 121-kilometer gravel road to the Chinese border via the Wakhan Corridor. While attention focuses on the Wakhjir Pass, the road's impact on the ethnic Kyrgyz in the Little Pamir, supported by Kyrgyzstan since 2008, is a less visible concern. Kyrgyzstan's policy aims to resettle this community as the road increases its strategic relevance.
